source.name: Hand-built, checked row by row against English Wikipedia

prize.pick: Which Nobel Prize did {label} win in {year}?
prize.statement: {label} won the Nobel Prize in {value} in {year}.
prize.odd: Three of these won the Nobel Prize in {value}. Which one didn't?
prize.all: Tap all {n} winners of the Nobel Prize in {value}.
prize.match: Match each laureate to their Nobel Prize.

year.sort: from the longest ago to the most recent
year.shot: In what year did {label} win the Nobel Prize in {prize}, {context}?

rows.label: Albert Einstein
rows.context: for explaining the photoelectric effect
rows.hook: explained how light can knock electrons loose from a metal, a discovery behind quantum theory

rows.label: Theodore Roosevelt
rows.context: for helping end the Russo-Japanese War
rows.description: 26th President of the United States from 1901 to 1909 (1858–1919)
rows.hook: helped broker the treaty that ended a war between Russia and Japan

rows.label: Ernest Hemingway
rows.context: for his spare, powerful storytelling
rows.hook: wrote spare, punchy novels about war, love and grace under pressure

rows.label: Bob Dylan
rows.context: for poetry in American songwriting
rows.hook: turned folk and rock songwriting into verse worthy of the great poets

rows.label: Jimmy Carter
rows.context: for decades of peace-building and human-rights work
rows.description: president of the United States from 1977 to 1981 (1924–2024)
rows.hook: spent decades after his presidency brokering deals and fighting disease worldwide

rows.label: Marie Curie
rows.context: for pioneering research on radioactivity
rows.hook: discovered new radioactive elements and became the first person honored twice for scientific work

rows.label: Martin Luther King Jr.
rows.context: for nonviolent civil-rights campaigning
rows.description: American Baptist minister and civil rights leader (1929–1968)
rows.hook: led the nonviolent campaign for civil rights that changed a nation's laws

rows.label: Nelson Mandela
rows.context: for his part in ending apartheid peacefully
rows.description: President of South Africa and anti-apartheid activist (1918–2013)
rows.hook: spent 27 years in prison before leading his country out of apartheid without a civil war

rows.label: Mother Teresa
rows.context: for her work with the poor in Kolkata
rows.hook: devoted her life to caring for the poorest and dying in the slums of Kolkata

rows.label: John Steinbeck
rows.context: for novels about working people's lives
rows.hook: wrote unflinching novels about migrant workers struggling through hard times

rows.label: Malala Yousafzai
rows.context: for fighting for girls' right to go to school
rows.hook: survived a targeted shooting and kept demanding that girls be allowed to go to school

rows.label: Geoffrey Hinton
rows.context: for machine learning with artificial neural networks
rows.hook: helped invent the neural-network methods that power today's AI systems

rows.label: Richard Feynman
rows.context: for work on quantum electrodynamics
rows.hook: cracked open the strange rules of how light and matter interact

rows.label: Albert Camus
rows.context: for novels and essays on life's absurdity
rows.hook: wrote philosophical novels wrestling with an absurd, indifferent universe

rows.label: Rudyard Kipling
rows.context: for his stories and verse
rows.hook: wrote colorful tales and verse set across the far corners of the British Empire

rows.label: Demis Hassabis
rows.context: for predicting protein shapes with AI
rows.hook: led the AI project that predicted the 3D shapes of nearly every known protein

rows.label: John Nash
rows.context: for game theory and how rivals reach a balance
rows.hook: worked out the math of how competing players settle into a stable standoff

rows.label: William Faulkner
rows.context: for his novels of the American South
rows.hook: wrote sprawling, experimental novels of a fictional Mississippi county

rows.label: Quakers
rows.context: for relief work during and after the world wars
rows.hook: operated relief networks that fed and sheltered refugees during two world wars

rows.label: Rabindranath Tagore
rows.context: for his poetry; the first non-European winner
rows.hook: wrote deeply spiritual poetry that opened the West's eyes to Indian verse and song

rows.label: Gabriel García Márquez
rows.context: for his novels of magical realism
rows.hook: wrote sprawling novels where a small town's history blurs into myth and magic

rows.label: Kazuo Ishiguro
rows.context: for quiet novels about memory and loss
rows.hook: wrote quiet, precise novels about memory, regret and the stories people tell themselves

rows.label: Toni Morrison
rows.context: for novels of African-American life
rows.description: African American novelist, essayist, and academic (1931–2019)
rows.hook: wrote powerful novels giving voice to the Black American experience

rows.label: T. S. Eliot
rows.context: for groundbreaking modern poetry
rows.hook: wrote dense, fragmented modern poetry that reshaped 20th-century verse

rows.label: Werner Heisenberg
rows.context: for creating quantum mechanics
rows.description: German theoretical physicist and nobel prize winner (1901–1976)
rows.hook: worked out the uncertainty at the heart of how tiny particles behave

rows.label: Thomas Mann
rows.context: for novels of German family and society
rows.description: German novelist and Nobel Prize laureate (1875–1955)
rows.hook: wrote sweeping novels about a fading family and a mountain sanatorium of ideas

rows.label: Niels Bohr
rows.context: for his model of how atoms are built
rows.hook: figured out how electrons orbit the atom in fixed, jumping steps

rows.label: Milton Friedman
rows.context: for work on consumption and the history of money
rows.hook: argued that steady control of the money supply matters more than any other policy lever

rows.label: George Bernard Shaw
rows.context: for his witty stage plays
rows.hook: wrote biting, witty plays that skewered class and social hypocrisy

rows.label: Samuel Beckett
rows.context: for plays such as Waiting for Godot
rows.hook: wrote stark, absurd plays where characters wait and talk to fill an empty world

rows.label: Desmond Tutu
rows.context: for nonviolent opposition to apartheid
rows.description: South African churchman, politician, archbishop, Nobel Prize winner (1931–2021)
rows.hook: used his pulpit to speak out against apartheid without ever turning to violence

rows.label: C. V. Raman
rows.context: for discovering how light scatters in materials
rows.hook: discovered how light changes color when it scatters through a liquid

rows.label: W. B. Yeats
rows.context: for poetry rooted in Irish tradition
rows.hook: wrote lyrical poetry steeped in Irish myth and the fight for independence

rows.label: Kofi Annan
rows.context: for his work towards a stronger United Nations
rows.hook: led the United Nations through some of its toughest humanitarian crises

rows.label: Hermann Hesse
rows.context: for novels such as Siddhartha
rows.description: Nobel Prize winning German-Swiss poet, novelist and painter (1877–1962)
rows.hook: wrote introspective novels tracing a search for spiritual meaning

rows.label: Erwin Schrödinger
rows.context: for his wave equation in quantum theory
rows.hook: wrote the equation that describes how a particle's wave behaves over time

rows.label: Alexander Fleming
rows.context: for discovering penicillin
rows.description: Scottish biologist, pharmacologist, botanist, and Nobel laureate (1881–1955)
rows.hook: noticed a stray mold killing bacteria and gave the world its first antibiotic

rows.label: Elie Wiesel
rows.context: for speaking out against hatred and violence
rows.description: Romanian-born American writer, professor, political activist, Nobel laureate, and Holocaust survivor (1928-2016)
rows.hook: survived the Holocaust and spent his life bearing witness against hatred and genocide

rows.label: Eugene O'Neill
rows.context: for his American stage dramas
rows.hook: wrote raw, tragic dramas that brought serious American theatre to the stage

rows.label: Roger Penrose
rows.context: for showing relativity predicts black holes
rows.description: English mathematical physicist, recreational mathematician and philosopher
rows.hook: proved that general relativity's own equations force black holes to form

rows.label: Dag Hammarskjöld
rows.context: for his peacekeeping work at the United Nations
rows.hook: led United Nations peacekeeping missions into some of Africa's toughest conflicts

rows.label: Ernest Rutherford
rows.context: for studying how radioactive elements break down
rows.hook: figured out that radioactive atoms transform into different elements as they decay

rows.label: George Marshall
rows.context: for the Marshall Plan that rebuilt Europe
rows.hook: designed the plan that rebuilt a shattered Europe after the second world war

rows.label: Enrico Fermi
rows.context: for nuclear reactions made with slow neutrons
rows.hook: built the reactor that produced the first controlled nuclear chain reaction

rows.label: Friedrich Hayek
rows.context: for work on money and the ups and downs of economies
rows.hook: argued that free markets, not central planners, best coordinate a complex economy

rows.label: Max Planck
rows.context: for discovering that energy comes in quanta
rows.hook: showed that energy comes in tiny indivisible packets, launching a whole new science

rows.label: Amartya Sen
rows.context: for work on welfare, poverty and famine
rows.hook: reshaped how the world measures poverty, famine and human wellbeing

rows.label: Willy Brandt
rows.context: for easing tension between East and West Europe
rows.description: German politician (SPD), chancellor of West Germany (1969–1974) and Nobel Peace Prize laureate
rows.hook: pushed for détente and reconciliation between a divided East and West Europe

rows.label: Doris Lessing
rows.context: for her novels about women's lives
rows.description: British novelist, poet, playwright, librettist, biographer, and short story writer (1919–2013)
rows.hook: wrote unflinching novels exploring women's inner lives and social upheaval

rows.label: Lech Wałęsa
rows.context: for leading Poland's Solidarity trade union
rows.hook: led a shipyard strike that grew into the movement that toppled communist rule

rows.label: Guglielmo Marconi
rows.context: for developing wireless telegraphy
rows.hook: sent the first wireless signals across the Atlantic Ocean

rows.label: Daniel Kahneman
rows.context: for bringing psychology into economic decisions
rows.hook: showed how everyday snap judgments quietly bend the way people make decisions

rows.label: Daron Acemoğlu
rows.context: for showing how institutions shape a nation's wealth
rows.description: Turkish-American economist and receiver of the 2024 Nobel Prize in economic sciences (born 1967)
rows.hook: traced how a nation's institutions decide whether it grows rich or stays poor

rows.label: Paul Dirac
rows.context: for new equations of quantum theory
rows.hook: wrote the equation that predicted antimatter before anyone had seen it

rows.label: Harold Pinter
rows.context: for his tense, pause-filled plays
rows.hook: wrote tense plays built on menacing silences and unfinished sentences

rows.label: James Watson
rows.context: for discovering the structure of DNA
rows.description: American molecular biologist, geneticist, zoologist and Nobel Laureate (1928–2025)
rows.hook: helped work out the double-helix shape that carries every living thing's genetic code

rows.label: Max Born
rows.context: for his work on quantum mechanics
rows.hook: worked out how to read a particle's wavefunction as pure probability

rows.label: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
rows.context: for working out how stars evolve
rows.hook: calculated the mass limit above which a dying star collapses into a black hole

rows.label: Jennifer Doudna
rows.context: for developing CRISPR gene editing
rows.hook: helped invent a tool that lets scientists edit genes with pinpoint precision

rows.label: J. J. Thomson
rows.context: for studying how electricity passes through gas
rows.hook: discovered the electron, the first subatomic particle ever found

rows.label: Mario Vargas Llosa
rows.context: for his novels of Latin American life
rows.description: Peruvian, Spanish and Dominican novelist and writer (1936–2025)
rows.hook: wrote novels exploring power, corruption and daily life across Latin America

rows.label: Han Kang
rows.context: for novels such as The Vegetarian
rows.hook: wrote piercing novels confronting trauma and violence in South Korean history

rows.label: Olga Tokarczuk
rows.context: for her imaginative, wide-ranging novels
rows.hook: writes boundary-crossing novels blending myth, history and fragmented storytelling

rows.label: Albert Schweitzer
rows.context: for his medical mission work in Africa
rows.description: French-German physician, theologian, musician, and philosopher (1875-1965)
rows.hook: gave up a life in music and theology to run a hospital for the poor in Africa

rows.label: Amnesty International
rows.context: for defending prisoners of conscience
rows.description: non-governmental organization based in the United Kingdom
rows.hook: campaigns worldwide to free prisoners jailed for their beliefs and expose human rights abuses

rows.label: Ivan Pavlov
rows.context: for research on how digestion works
rows.hook: trained dogs to drool at the sound of a bell, revealing how the body learns automatic responses

rows.label: Irène Joliot-Curie
rows.context: for making new radioactive elements
rows.hook: created new radioactive elements in the lab, building on her family's pioneering work in radioactivity

rows.label: Norman Borlaug
rows.context: for high-yield crops that fought world hunger
rows.hook: bred hardier, higher-yield wheat that is credited with saving millions of people from famine

rows.label: Pierre Curie
rows.context: for research on radioactivity
rows.hook: discovered how certain crystals generate electricity when squeezed, then studied radioactivity with his wife

rows.label: Sinclair Lewis
rows.context: for satirical novels of American life
rows.hook: wrote sharp satirical novels skewering small-town American conformity and hypocrisy

rows.label: Seamus Heaney
rows.context: for his poetry of Irish rural life
rows.hook: wrote poetry rooted in rural Irish life, land and folklore

rows.label: UNICEF
rows.context: for its work for children around the world
rows.description: specialised agency of the United Nations
rows.hook: works around the world to protect children's health, nutrition and education

rows.label: Pearl S. Buck
rows.context: for her novels of life in China
rows.description: Chinese women Nobel Prize winner, author, teacher, missionary (1892–1973)
rows.hook: wrote novels bringing Chinese peasant life to Western readers

rows.label: Jane Addams
rows.context: for social reform and peace work
rows.description: American feminist social activist, reformer, social worker, sociologist, philosopher, and writer (1860–1935)
rows.hook: co-founded a settlement house helping immigrants and championed social reform

rows.label: Wilhelm Röntgen
rows.context: for discovering X-rays
rows.hook: discovered a new kind of ray that could see through skin to reveal the bones beneath

rows.label: Kip Thorne
rows.context: for helping detect gravitational waves
rows.hook: helped build the detector that first sensed ripples in space-time from colliding black holes

rows.label: Saul Bellow
rows.context: for his novels of modern American life
rows.hook: wrote novels of restless, intellectual characters navigating modern American cities

rows.label: Yasunari Kawabata
rows.context: for his novels of Japanese life
rows.hook: wrote spare, lyrical novels capturing beauty and loss in Japanese life

rows.label: Orhan Pamuk
rows.context: for his novels set in Istanbul
rows.description: Turkish novelist, academic and Nobel laureate (born 1952)
rows.hook: wrote novels steeped in the clashing history and identity of a city straddling two continents

rows.label: Francis Crick
rows.context: for discovering the structure of DNA
rows.description: British molecular biologist, biophysicist, neuroscientist; co-discoverer of the structure of DNA (1916–2004)
rows.hook: helped work out the double-helix shape of the molecule that carries genetic information

rows.label: Lester B. Pearson
rows.context: for the UN force that calmed the Suez Crisis
rows.description: 14th Prime Minister of Canada, from 1963 to 1968 (1897–1972)
rows.hook: organized a UN peacekeeping force credited with defusing a major Middle East crisis

rows.label: Wangari Maathai
rows.context: for tree planting and sustainable development
rows.description: Kenyan environmentalist and politician who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2004 (1940–2011)
rows.hook: founded a movement that had ordinary women plant tens of millions of trees to fight deforestation

rows.label: Tu Youyou
rows.context: for finding a new treatment for malaria
rows.hook: discovered a plant-based compound that became a life-saving treatment for malaria

rows.label: Robert Koch
rows.context: for research on tuberculosis
rows.hook: identified the bacteria responsible for tuberculosis and other deadly diseases

rows.label: Andrei Sakharov
rows.context: for speaking out for human rights in the USSR
rows.description: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
rows.hook: helped build his country's most powerful weapon, then spent decades campaigning for human rights

rows.label: Médecins Sans Frontières
rows.context: for emergency medical aid around the world
rows.hook: sends volunteer doctors and nurses into war zones and disaster areas to treat anyone in need
